subject: Model shortlist & initial capacity estimates for Grace Analytics onboarding
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Rudd <maya.rudd@grace-analytics.com>; ops@grace-analytics.com
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Model shortlist & quick sizing for onboarding (first pass)

Hi Maya / Grace team —

Thanks again for the call today. Per promise, I wanted to surface a pragmatic model shortlist and an initial capacity sketch so your engineers can plan infra and integration work. This is a first-pass estimate; Stephanie will coordinate the handoff and finalize the playbook.

Quick context: your MVP uses two main flows — (A) multi-turn analyst-assistant chat (average 6 turns, heavy context), and (B) high-throughput single-turn summarization for batch reports. You mentioned typical document length ~8–12k characters and 2–3 queries per document.

Model shortlist (recommended order for evaluation):
- Mistral-Instruct-7B-32k (quantized) — good instruction-following, lower cost for high-volume summarization; 32k context for long docs.
- Llama-2-Chat-70B-8k (opt) — best for nuanced chat quality; higher latency/cost, useful for premium users and SLO-driven routes.
- Vicuna-13B-16k (custom-tuned) — balance of quality and cost for mid-tier chat.

Initial token volume / sizing assumptions (please confirm):
- Active users (MVP): 3,000 daily active users generating ~1 request/day on average.
- Chat flow: avg prompt+history ~4,500 tokens, avg response ~600 tokens => ~5,100 tokens per chat request. Estimated chat QPS: peak 20 QPS, 95th percentile concurrency ~35 in short bursts.
- Summarization flow: batch jobs ~200/day, avg prompt+input ~15,000 tokens, responses ~1,200 tokens — batching reduces per-token overhead.

Rough cost/perf guidance (production target):
- Start with Dedicated pool: 4 x A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved) to meet latency SLOs for chat and to have headroom for batching on summarization.
- Autoscale/burst to hosted capacity for peak-heavy batch windows.
- Use prefix/KV caching for repeated context across turns to save tokens where possible.

Attachments: I attached the sample context file you shared (grace_ops_context_examples.txt) and a short initial calc. Stephanie — can you pick this up and convert into a playbook for the onboarding runbook?

Next steps:
1) Stephanie: confirm final model shortlist and produce a 2-week rollout playbook (integration checklist + gating evals).
2) Grace: confirm daily expected doc volumes & any 32k-context use cases that must be supported day 1.
3) Sergio: coordinate commercial sizing / quote based on dedicated pool above.

Thanks —
Sergio
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Maya Rudd <maya.rudd@grace-analytics.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@grace-analytics.com, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 09:02:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Model shortlist & quick sizing for onboarding (first pass)

Sergio / Stephanie —

Thanks for the clear write-up. A few clarifications from ops: 
- The 8–12k character note maps to roughly 3–4k tokens in our pipeline, but we have a small subset (~10% of docs) that are long-form extracts pushing toward 20k tokens. Those are the ones we flagged for 32k context.
- Expected daily volumes: currently 4,500 unique documents processed/day with ~2.5 queries per doc (some of those are automated batch summarizations). Peak processing windows are nightly (02:00–04:00 local).
- SLA desires: 95% responses < 700ms for interactive chat flows; batch can be longer.

We can share a sample of our document breakdown (attached). If 4 x A100 is the starting point, can you sketch expected QPS and per-GPU load for both the chat and summarization workloads? Also clarify whether Redwood’s caching will materially reduce token counts for the chat use-case (we do see repeated references across a session).

Appreciate it —
Maya Rudd
Head of Ops, Grace Analytics
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Rudd <maya.rudd@grace-analytics.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Model shortlist & quick sizing for onboarding (first pass)

Hi Maya —

Great details, thanks. I pulled the numbers into a quick-capacity calc (attached initial_capacity_calc.xlsx) and sketched an actionable onboarding playbook (grace_mvp_playbook.pdf) so your engineers can coordinate testing with our infra team. High-level answers below.

1) QPS / GPU assumptions (first-pass):
- Mistral-7B-32k (quantized) — approx 160 tokens/sec per GPU effective decoding for summarization workloads when batched; with nightly batching we expect a single GPU can handle ~120 batch jobs/hour depending on batch sizes.
- Llama-2-Chat-70B-8k — interactive latency target ~350–600ms per response at 95th on A100-class hardware when concurrency is moderate; one GPU supports ~12–16 interactive QPS for high-quality 70B chat (lower with long history).
- Vicuna-13B-16k — about ~35–45 interactive QPS per GPU with 95th latency ~250–450ms.

2) Caching impact:
- Prefix / KV cache: for chat where a high fraction of context is repeated (system prompt, instructions, and earlier turns), KV caching can save ~25–40% of compute/tokens on subsequent tokens. If your sessions reuse prompts heavily, enable KV cache early.

3) Suggested initial infra profile:
- Dedicated pool: 2 x A100 for chat (primary low-latency routing: Llama-70B + Vicuna-13B can be split by tier), 2 x A100 for batch/summarization using Mistral-7B-32k with aggressive batching.
- Reserve headroom for bursts: allow autoscale to add 2 GPUs from hosted pool for peak windows.
- Start with this and iterate after 2 weeks of traffic when we can observe real token counts and tail latencies.

4) Integration checklist highlights:
- Provide sample traffic (we received grace_ops_context_examples.txt) and a small eval prompt set for quality gating.
- Instrument token-level metrics (we'll provide SDK trace hooks) and enable per-route SLOs.
- Decide rollout: canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 7–10 days.

Action items (stephanie):
- I will schedule a 60-minute handoff with your infra lead next week to walk through playbook and run the first validation.
- Evelyn, please prepare an operations runbook for incident response during the initial 14-day ramp.

Maya — can you confirm a 60-minute slot Tuesday 03/02 or Wednesday 03/03 PST?

Thanks —
Stephanie Nguyen
Technical Program Manager, Onboarding | Redwood Inference
From: Maya Rudd <maya.rudd@grace-analytics.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@grace-analytics.com
Date: Mon, 01 Mar 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model shortlist & quick sizing for onboarding (first pass)

Stephanie / Sergio —

Thanks — Tuesday 03/02 at 10:00 PST works for our infra lead (I added the calendar invite). We reviewed the playbook PDF and the initial calc looks reasonable. A couple quick notes before the call:
- We confirmed ~4,500 docs/day and 2.5 queries/doc as noted. Expect ~10% long-docs that need 32k context day 1.
- For the canary, we want to route low-risk accounts to Mistral-7B-32k and premium accounts to Llama-70B-8k. Can you add a routing policy sketch to the playbook?

Looking forward to the call.

Best —
Maya
Head of Ops, Grace Analytics
